messages:
devon (Devon R.): Heads up — we're seeing a sustained latency spike and throughput drop in dedicated-eu-west. 99p token latency jumped from ~110ms to ~620ms around 21:12 UTC, overall throughput down ~30%. Customers are hitting SLO alerts. 

maria (Maria L.): ack. any idea on root cause? noisy tenant / kernel mismatch?

devon (Devon R.): early traces point to placement churn + quota misconfig. pool-42 got overcommitted after a recent capacity shift; kernels fell back to a slower aten kernel for many small-seq requests which amplified kv-cache churn. profiling attached below.

alex (Alex C.): can you paste the profiler snippet?

devon (Devon R.): ```
[21:11:58] pool-42: active_slots=96/96, evictions/sec=48, kv-cache-hit=0.31, batch-size-mean=1.3
[21:12:02] kernel-select: chosen=aten_fused (fallback) for model:gpt-xl seq=32, reason=kernel-pool-mismatch
[21:12:05] scheduler: queue-latency-ms=220, token-latency-ms=580
```

nora (Nora S.): kv-cache-hit 0.31 is brutal — working set overflow. are these tenants generating many short prompts?

devon (Devon R.): yes + a sudden onboarding of a large tenant that was assigned to pool-42 (quota policy mis-evaluated by placement service). they had high cache locality previously, now evicted and thrashing.

infra-bot: placement-service: recent deploy 21:09 UTC — change: respect_legacy_quota=false flagged for eu-west rollout.

maria (Maria L.): that flag rings a bell. previous tests had a bug where reserved_quota was effectively ignored when affinity_score<0.2. Can we patch placement to respect reserved_quota immediately?

alex (Alex C.): short-term mitigation: 1) isolate the noisy tenant (move to dedicated-isolation node), 2) bump pool capacity by shifting two standby nodes into pool-42, 3) force kernel pinning for hot model versions to fused kernels. Any objections?

sre-oncall: doing 1 & 2 now. moving tenant foo-33 off pool-42 -> ETA 60s.

nora (Nora S.): for 3 we need to ensure quantized kernels are compatible; pinning might increase CPU/GPU mem slightly but should drop token latency. I'll prepare a canary config.

devon (Devon R.): running a quick experiment: enabling prefix-KV sticky-cache for pool-42 to reduce cold cache misses. Applying in 30s.

infra-bot: cluster: node-shift start -> nodes moved: eu-n1-07, eu-n1-08 into pool-42

maria (Maria L.): patch to placement rolled back at 21:18 UTC; will open PR to fix reserved_quota semantics and add unit test.

devon (Devon R.): after tenant move + node shift + sticky-cache, 21:22 UTC metrics: 99p latency down to ~180ms, throughput recovered to ~92% baseline, kv-cache-hit up to 0.78. Looks promising.

alex (Alex C.): good. action items: 
- maria: hotfix placement reserved_quota semantics + add regression test (priority P0)
- nora: validate kernel pin config + schedule canary across 5% traffic (P0)
- devon: add alert for kv-cache-hit < 0.5 on dedicated pools (P1)
- sre-oncall: follow up with customer ops about SLA blips and RCA timeline (P1)

maria (Maria L.): will cut the hotfix PR now and request expedited review.

sre-oncall: notified impacted customers at 21:30 UTC, asking if any want immediate credits.

devon (Devon R.): quick note for postmortem — root cause chain: placement feature flag + reserved_quota regression -> noisy tenant co-located with several hot small-seq workloads -> kernel fallback due to kernel-pool mismatch -> high eviction rate and KV cache thrash -> latency/throughput regression and SLA alerts.

nora (Nora S.): also add: batching heuristics need improvement for mixed-size workloads. current continuous batching favors small batch-size due to many single-turn requests, causing higher kernel dispatch overhead and less efficient kernel choice. I'll draft a perf proposal to bias batching for stable minibatches for 2+ seqs.

alex (Alex C.): noted. we'll schedule a follow-up perf review with runtime and placement teams tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

devon (Devon R.): closing thread: metrics stable for 20m, continuing monitoring. will file incident postmortem and link to this thread. :white_check_mark:
